methodology: Manual scholarly web inspection of online full-work English translations. Each locus must identify the real work and a matching argument, while variants and cited chapter boundaries are documented; no claim of Greek/Latin critical collation.
translationNotice: Oxford/Newman Catena fragments and separate NPNF-era whole-work English translations may differ: neither text has been replaced or silently conflated.

records.originalReaderQuestion: What does Scripture mean by calling certain men the Lord's brothers?
records.patristicWork: Jerome, De perpetua virginitate Beatae Mariae adversus Helvidium
records.workLocus: Chapters 16–17 (Catena abbreviation labels cont. Helvid. 14 et seq.)
records.translatedParallelEvidence: Jerome gives four senses of 'brethren'—nature, race, kindred and affection—and rejects the interpretation as additional sons of Mary.
records.qualification: Crucial boundary: the fuller argument appears across chapters 16–17 in the online English translation; the Catena's label '14 et seq.' is not a one-chapter citation, and Helvidius's position is quoted as an objection.

records.originalReaderQuestion: Why does the sower scatter seed on apparently unfruitful ground?
records.translatedParallelEvidence: The sower does not desist merely because some soil fails; Chrysostom contrasts rocky fields with mutable souls.
records.qualification: The Catena abbreviates the homily, and the New Advent translation is a distinct English witness. Precise homily-section locator independently corrected by re-reading the online full work on 2026-10-22.

records.originalReaderQuestion: How does the net parable differ from the tares and the sower?
records.translatedParallelEvidence: Direct comparison of tares, sower and fishing net; wicked doctrines, inattentive hearing and evil life remain separate categories.
records.qualification: Avoid presenting the three metaphors as interchangeable or as a unified modern doctrinal formula.

records.originalReaderQuestion: How does Augustine reconcile who asked the Sabbath-healing question in the Synoptics?
records.patristicWork: Augustine, De consensu evangelistarum (Harmony of the Gospels)
records.translatedParallelEvidence: The opponents' Sabbath question is hypothesized first; Jesus then addresses his own question to them as Mark and Luke report.
records.qualification: Augustine proposes a harmonization of narrative sequence, not independently established dialogue chronology.

records.originalReaderQuestion: Why did Christ lead the disciples through grainfields on the Sabbath?
records.translatedParallelEvidence: The hunger of the disciples is a necessity distinguished from a manifest sin; Chrysostom explains Christ's deliberate teaching on Sabbath observance.
records.qualification: The translated homily uses language about breaking the Sabbath and then immediately qualifies guilt; preserve the full argument rather than suggesting Christ acted sinfully.

records.originalReaderQuestion: Why did Christ speak of the Pharisees' leaven rather than their doctrine outright?
records.translatedParallelEvidence: Chrysostom asks why Christ did not plainly warn about doctrine and answers by the disciples' forgetfulness after the loaves.
records.qualification: Retain the surrounding rebuke and bread miracle sequence.

records.originalReaderQuestion: How can the omnipresent Christ be said to go out to sow?
records.translatedParallelEvidence: The Sower goes out in the Incarnation, not by changing physical location; the same original homily treats the sower's soil.
records.qualification: The change of location is expressly denied. Do not imply divine absence or limited omnipresence.

records.originalReaderQuestion: Does conception by the Holy Spirit make the Holy Spirit Christ's Father?
records.patristicWork: Augustine, Enchiridion ad Laurentium (Handbook on Faith, Hope and Love)
records.translatedParallelEvidence: Chapter 38 rejects calling the Holy Spirit Christ's Father; chapter 39 explains that being born 'of' something does not make one its son.
records.qualification: Catena cites chapter 38 but its condensed passage contains reasoning explicitly continuing into chapter 39 of the full work; preserve the chapter span.

records.originalReaderQuestion: Does Matthew's word 'until' imply that Joseph and Mary later had marital relations?
records.patristicWork: Jerome, De perpetua virginitate Beatae Mariae adversus Helvidium (Against Helvidius)
records.translatedParallelEvidence: Jerome reports Helvidius's inference from 'until' and distinguishes scriptural uses without allowing it to imply a change after Christ's birth.
records.qualification: The Catena's condensed excerpt draws argumentation spanning chapters 5–8; Helvidius's assertions are objections, not Jerome's convictions.

records.originalReaderQuestion: How does Augustine explain the ease of Christ's yoke amid hardships?
records.workLocus: Sermon 70, sections 1–2; NPNF New Testament Sermon 20
records.translatedParallelEvidence: Augustine contrasts the apparent hardship of discipleship with divine love, interior renewal and the expectation of future rest.
records.qualification: The web edition calls it 'Sermon 20 on the New Testament' while the Catena identifies 'Sermon 70'; these are different numbering systems, not different authors.

records.originalReaderQuestion: How do the priests' Sabbath duties answer the accusation against the disciples?
records.translatedParallelEvidence: Chrysostom explicitly contrasts David's one-off emergency with the priests' repeated lawful temple work on the Sabbath.
records.qualification: The priestly service is not condemned as sinful; the Lord of the Temple and the differing occasions supply the qualifications.

records.originalReaderQuestion: How can harvest mean both the present mission and the end of the world?
records.translatedParallelEvidence: Chrysostom compares fields already white for harvesting among the Samaritans with the final harvest of Matthew 13.
records.qualification: Do not erase the distinction between initial conversion and judgment at the end of the world. Precise homily-section locator independently corrected by re-reading the online full work on 2026-10-22.

records.originalReaderQuestion: Do Matthew and John's descriptions of Christ withdrawing to a mountain contradict?
records.patristicWork: Augustine, De consensu evangelistarum (Harmony of the Gospels)
records.translatedParallelEvidence: Augustine interprets Matthew and John's mountain references alongside the disciples' embarkation and Christ's prior command.
records.qualification: Interpretive Gospel harmonization; not an independent reconstruction of chronology.

records.originalReaderQuestion: Did the Magi's star govern Christ's fate or serve Him?
records.translatedParallelEvidence: The Magi's star is subordinate to Christ rather than governing his fate; Augustine disputes the Manichaean objection and astrological fatalism.
records.qualification: Preserve the adversarial context against Faustus; this is patristic theological reasoning, not an astronomical identification.

records.originalReaderQuestion: How does Hilary answer interpretations that divide the divine and human in Christ?
records.translatedParallelEvidence: Hilary attributes mistaken views about the Son's divine and human natures to opponents, then interprets the Cross while insisting on one Christ, God and man.
records.qualification: The Catena compresses nonadjacent parts of Hilary's longer argument: §§50–52 describe rejected positions and §§60–62 give the positive explanation; never present heretical speech as Hilary's confession.

records.originalReaderQuestion: How does Jerome answer Helvidius concerning the women at the Cross and Christ's brethren?
records.patristicWork: Jerome, De perpetua virginitate Beatae Mariae adversus Helvidium
records.translatedParallelEvidence: Jerome argues against Helvidius by distinguishing Mary the mother of James and Joses, Mary of Clopas and the Mother of the Lord.
records.qualification: Helvidius's reported arguments and Jerome's rebuttal span several chapters and speaker positions; do not assume every sentence in the condensed Catena quote belongs to Jerome as a positive claim.

records.originalReaderQuestion: How does Augustine reconcile Matthew's evening with Mark's early morning at the tomb?
records.patristicWork: Augustine, De consensu evangelistarum (Harmony of the Gospels)
records.translatedParallelEvidence: Augustine explicitly reads Matthew's 'evening' as the night taken as a whole, terminating at the dawn referred to by Mark.
records.qualification: Preserve Bede's neighboring, distinct interpretative explanation as an alternative rather than falsely merging them.

records.originalReaderQuestion: How does Chrysostom refute the allegation that the disciples stole Christ's body?
records.translatedParallelEvidence: Chrysostom counters the body-theft allegation through fear, the guards and seal, and the burial linens and myrrh.
records.qualification: A patristic apologetic argument; confirmation of where the argument occurs does not establish its premises as modern forensic facts.
